steps.message:
Before I touch it: this is a breaking change to a published contract, not just a rename.

`routes/users.js:6` emits `userId` in the `GET /users` response body. Renaming it there changes what every client parses. The README names the consumers:

> Consumers of `GET /users`: the web app, the iOS app (3.2 and later), and the nightly partner export. Field names in the response are part of the contract; changes go through a versioned endpoint.

So a straight rename breaks any client still reading `userId` — notably shipped iOS builds you can't update in lockstep, and the partner export. The README also states the project's own rule that this kind of change goes through a versioned endpoint.

I'd like your call before editing.

questions.question: How should the userId -> user_id rename on GET /users be handled?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId for a deprecation window, so existing clients keep working while new ones move to user_id. Smallest change that doesn't break anyone; you drop userId later.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README rule: leave GET /users as-is and expose the snake_case shape on a new version (e.g. /v2/users). Cleanest contract story, more work.

options.label: Straight rename anyway
options.description: Replace userId with user_id in place. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS 3.2+ builds, and the nightly partner export until each is updated.
